### Srimad Bhagavad Gita

<meta>continues from the previous page: discussion of the impartiality of God regarding His devotees.</meta>

<note>Commentary by Sridhara Swami:</note>
If you grant liberation only to devotees and not to non-devotees, does that not imply you possess partiality born of attachment and aversion? He answers this in the negative with the verse beginning with "I am equal." I am equal toward all beings; therefore, to Me, there is no one particularly dear or hateful. Even so, those who worship Me with devotion, those devotees abide in Me, and I also abide in them as their benefactor. The idea is this: just as fire removes the distress of darkness and cold only for those who serve <note>stay near</note> it, yet the fire itself possesses no partiality; or just as a wish-fulfilling tree <term>kalpavriksha</term> <gloss>a divine tree that grants all desires</gloss> acts similarly; in the same way, although I favor My devotees, I have no partiality. Rather, this is the glorious power of devotion to Me. (Verse 29)

<note>Commentary by Madhusudana Sarasvati:</note>
Furthermore, listen to the greatness of devotion to Me, which creates the appearance of partiality even in One who is equal:

> Even if a man of very wicked conduct worships Me with undivided devotion,
> he must be considered righteous, for he has rightly resolved. (Verse 30)

If anyone, even one of very wicked conduct like <term>Ajamila</term> <gloss>a legendary sinner who was saved by calling the name of God at death</gloss> and others, worships Me with undivided devotion due to some dawn of good fortune, he must be considered righteous, even if he was unrighteous before. This is because <note>as the text says "hi"</note> he has rightly resolved; he possesses the firm conviction of a saint. (Verse 30)

<note>Commentary by Sridhara Swami:</note>
Showing that the influence of devotion to Me is inconceivable, He says "Even if": Even a man of extremely wicked conduct, if he worships Me, Lord Narayana, without practicing devotion to other deities separately, then he must be considered as someone excellent <note>a saint</note>. Because he has "rightly resolved"—he has made the beautiful determination that "I shall achieve my life's purpose simply by worshiping the Supreme Lord." (Verse 30)

<note>Commentary by Madhusudana Sarasvati:</note>
Because of this right resolution, having abandoned his wicked conduct:

> Quickly he becomes a righteous soul and attains eternal peace.
> O son of Kunti <note>Arjuna</note>, know for certain: My devotee never perishes. (Verse 31)

Even if he was an unrighteous soul for a long time, through the greatness of worshiping Me, he "quickly"—very soon—becomes a righteous soul <term>dharmatma</term> <gloss>one whose mind follows virtue</gloss>. The meaning is that by immediately abandoning wicked conduct, he becomes a man of good conduct. Furthermore, he "attains eternal peace"—he completely reaches the cessation of the desire for sense objects through extreme detachment. To the doubt that "some devotee of Mine might not become a righteous soul because he does not give up previously practiced wicked conduct, and thus he might perish," the Lord says "No," as if He were angry out of His extreme compassion for His devotees: "O son of Kunti, do not think this is a wonder; such is the greatness of devotion to Me. Therefore, even in the presence of those who disagree, you should declare it; make a proud and bold proclamation: 'The devotee of Me, Vasudeva, even if he is very wicked in conduct, even if his life is in danger, even if he is sought after for something very rare, even if he is a complete fool or without refuge, he never perishes; rather, he achieves his life's purpose.'"

<summary>The text explains that God is impartial toward all, but devotion creates a special bond that redeems even the most wicked sinners. It emphasizes that a firm resolve to worship God quickly transforms an individual's character and ensures they never perish spiritually.</summary>
<keywords>impartiality of God, devotion, bhakti, redemption, Ajamila, righteousness, dharmatma, Vasudeva, Krishna, Arjuna, spiritual transformation</keywords>
